entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Khadidiatou Diallo is a Senegalese advocate and the founder of the Groupe de femmes pour l'Abolition des Mutilations Sexuelles (GAMS) in Belgium. Born in the 1980s, Diallo has spent decades advocating for the rights of survivors of female genital mutilation (FGM) and pushing for the abolition of this practice in Senegal and beyond. Her work has been recognized internationally, earning her the title of 'Ambassador of the Girl Child' from the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

Diallo's efforts have been instrumental in shaping the conversation around FGM, which is practiced in several African countries, including Senegal. Her advocacy has led to the passage of laws and policies aimed at preventing and addressing FGM, including the 2018 Senegalese law that makes FGM punishable by law.

The impact of Diallo's work extends beyond Senegal, as she has worked closely with international organizations and governments to push for global action against FGM. Her efforts have been recognized by the African Union, which has acknowledged her contributions to the fight against FGM.

Despite the progress made, FGM remains a significant challenge in Senegal, with thousands of girls and women still at risk of undergoing the practice. Diallo's continued advocacy is crucial in addressing this issue and promoting the rights of survivors.

Diallo's legacy extends beyond her work on FGM, as she has also been a vocal advocate for women's rights and girls' education. Her commitment to these causes has inspired a new generation of activists and leaders in Senegal and beyond.
